Compared with stage2, successful immediate call counts match, receive bytes differ by9B, and194 more empty immediate IO attempts occur. retained_boundaries: Original raw protocol callbacks, status/headers/payload oracle,16KiB stream+connection consumption, paired reverse response rules and send/recv flags retained.
Both endpoint drivers use the original HyleHarness one-worker IoContext and spawn_task; inactive persistent RawHarness also constructed as in the original benchmark.
RawWire owns128KiB per endpoint outside the64KiB fiber stacks, Episode and native userdata live through both joins; reserved4 stream slots prevent pointer relocation.
Server waits only after last pair first response was submitted, its body provider is done and the endpoint pending wire is empty. Client signals after final response payload validation.

Endpoint cleanup destroys native session then resets TcpStream on its worker before returning. TcpStream move assignment calls synchronous ::close on Linux, so post-join fcntl EBADF does not depend on later IoContext drain.
Independent read-only review found no definite protocol/completion/owner-lifetime bug. No additional runtime was requested or executed.
limits: No durations or cost weights collected. Formal manual-loop peer remains the real comparator; its existing13-15% matched large-body loss is still unresolved.
Single episode with probe array writes/interposition perturbs scheduling; no fresh live thread/worker resource census and no universal runtime guarantee.
Driver is separately implemented from the Hyle protocol transport and has194 additional EAGAIN attempts; changes in syscall/codec/lifecycle work prevent pure scheduler attribution.
No claim that all yields are necessary, negligible, or account for any percentage. No cancellation/fairness/readiness/owner/completion responsibility removed.
